profiles.name: Nealyneal73
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file where the flatstick is doing all the damn emotional labor while the rest of the bag keeps tripping over its own feet. The irons have flashed enough pop to keep the card from being a crime scene, but the short game has also lit some rounds on fire in the ugliest way possible. When the putter’s hot, he can look sneaky dangerous; when it cools off, the rest of the setup isn’t stable enough to hide behind. Volatile, but not boring.

profiles.name: AdamBailey25
profiles.tagline: BALL-STRIKING, THEN A LOOSE STEERING WHEEL
profiles.profile: The weird part here is that the tee-to-green stuff keeps showing up like a guy who knows exactly where the fairway is and just chooses not to live there. There’s enough approach quality to build something real, but the scoring can still get mugged by the putter and the occasional sand-face mess. This is a mixed bag with a ceiling, not a clean profile: when the irons are sharp, it looks tidy; when they aren’t, the round turns into a slow leak and the putter doesn’t come save the ass.

profiles.name: Rhino
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GAME IN A GAS LEAK
profiles.profile: This profile is basically a tug-of-war between a putter trying to keep the house from burning down and an approach game kicking in the doors. The scoring can survive a little chaos if the putter stays alive, but the rest of the bag keeps handing out bogeys like sample cups at a range tent. There’s been enough short-game contribution to hint at a possible fix, but it’s still a pretty noisy file. Not dead yet, just one of those deals where the irons are loudly underperforming the resume.

profiles.name: StevieD
profiles.tagline: THE PUTTER IS COMMITTED TO THE BIT
profiles.profile: If the flatstick had any less help, this thing would be a full-on hostage situation. The profile has one clear theme: the putter keeps choosing violence for the wrong side, and the short game hasn’t been nearly reliable enough to cover for it. There was at least one round where the scoring shape looked salvageable, but the more recent damage was brutal enough to drag the whole file toward the basement. Mixed signals, sure, but the strongest signal is still ugly as hell.

profiles.name: CornBred89
profiles.profile: Tiny sample, giant goblin energy. The one completed look came with an eagle mixed into a pile of missed green-life and a putting line that didn’t do much to stop the bleeding, which is exactly the kind of weird little card that says more about volatility than talent. There’s not enough history here to crown a story, but the current read is simple: this bag can produce a cool shot or two while also making the scoring math look like it was done by a drunk raccoon.

profiles.name: BobNoWay
profiles.tagline: BOGEY BUDGET WITH A PUTTING TAX
profiles.profile: This is a pretty clean picture of a golfer who can find enough greens to keep things from totally collapsing, then promptly hands the gains back with way too many bogeys and a putter that doesn’t pay rent. The iron play hasn’t exactly been setting off fireworks, but the bigger issue is that the whole card keeps leaking strokes in bunches instead of just one stupid hole. There’s some survival skill here, but the file reads like a guy who keeps showing up to a knife fight with a butter knife and a receipt.
